newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Credit Lyonnais HK gets HK$.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Credit Lyonnais HK gets HK$.

text.p: The Hong Kong branch of French bank Credit Lyonnais launched a HK$1.0 billion floating rate certificate of deposit issue into Asian debt markets on Wednesday.
The three-year FRCDs were launched at par to float at 32 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return for the top tier is 40 basis points.
Credit Lyonnais and HSBC Markets are joint bookrunners.
Bankers said the pricing was "reasonable."
A few key factors count in the issue's favor, they said.
For one, application has been made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the certificates as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
The issuer is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service.
As a French bank, Credit Lyonnais debt qualifies for a 20 percent risk asset weighting under Bank for International Settlement rules regarding OECD country banks.
That means that lenders must set aside less in the form of provisioning then they would have to if the issuer was a Hong Kong-based bank, for example.

State-owned Credit Lyonnais is in the midst of a massive restructuring following huge losses in the early part of this decade. But it recently surprised financial markets by reporting a modest 1996 profit and a significantly improved underlying performance.
The French Finance Ministry said last Friday that it was on track to submit in early April a long-delayed privatisation plan for Credit Lyonnais to the European Commission.
Jean-Marc Winand, a syndicate manager at Credit Lyonnais in Hong Kong, said proceeds of the deal would be used to better match the Hong Kong branch's assets and liabilities.
Syndicate managers in Hong Kong noted that a number of banks in the territory are likely borrow long-term money to better match long-term liabilities, such as mortgage lending.
In other news, details emerged on the US$100 million floating rate note issue for Indonesian property developer PT Duta Anggada Reality.
The three-year notes pay a coupon of 275 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 325 basis points.
Union Bank of Switzerland is lead manager.
There was more news on Sun Hung Kai Properties HK$5.0 billion revolving credit/term loan facility.

Bankers said six banks -- Hang Seng Finance, Sumitomo Bank Hong Kong, Societe Generale Asia, Chase Manhattan Asia, BNP Hong Kong and Standard Chartered Bank -- have been mandated as coordinating arrangers.
The facility will launch through the company's subsidiary Sun Hung Kai Properties (Financial Services) Ltd. It carries a maturity of seven years and has an average life of 5.75 years.
